592450|2016: Judge has 410 AAA PA with 19 HR and 95 MLB PA with 42 strikeouts. The 2016 list adds rank 31, score .70, after rank 68 in 2015 and no 2014 top-100 listing. This rank can represent independent industry confidence despite a poor MLB debut, not a guaranteed 2017 job or a superstar batting grade.
641355|2016: Bellinger has 465 AA PA with 23 HR and 12 AAA PA with three HR, but none of the three preseason top lists contains him. Complete-list absence is a real listing fact, not proof of low talent. His published 2016 research-dataset report exists even though he is absent from this narrower ranking source; its grades/ETA stay withheld. This experiment cannot be sold as complete scouting or an answer to every fast mover. His production, age and draft evidence are retained rather than overwritten by the zero listing flag.

The incomplete 2021 list does not contain him, so both listed and score for that lag are unknown, not an unranked zero. The 2019 research-dataset grades cannot be silently promoted to a 2022 update. A strong upper-minor ranking is sensible readiness evidence to test, but next-year opportunity still depends on advancement and team choices.
701762|2024: Kurtz has only 35 A PA and 15 AA PA in his draft year, including four HR and twelve unintentional walks. The 2024 preseason ranking precedes his professional entry and has no listing. His draft pick remains in the baseline; absent preseason scouting must not be called a negative signing evaluation. The 2013–2019 research dataset cannot supply him a report. This locked source has no fresh post-draft ranking and may leave the known fast-entry gap unresolved. Do not manually add a rank from a later year.
808393|2024: Concepcion has 199 DSL PA, three HR, 61 strikeouts and 23 unintentional walks in 2024. He is absent from complete 2022–2024 top-100 lists and absent from the older research dataset. A top-100 supplement has much narrower coverage than the entire lower-minor population and cannot certify that population's talent model.
621446|2016: Brinson's source has 326 AA PA with eleven HR, 93 AAA PA with four HR and fifteen rookie PA. Rank 16 adds strong industry confidence despite a limited AAA sample. He is an important opposite case to successful high-ranked prospects: rankings describe prospects with uncertainty, not guaranteed realized batting value. The publisher entity contains several report years, including later ones; the model receives rank only. The retrospective table agrees on 16 while a dated launch narrative says 14, so exact publication-time rank is qualified rather than asserted identical across sources.
640449|2016: Frazier has 391 AA PA with thirteen HR and 129 AAA PA with three HR and 36 strikeouts. Rank 27, score .74, supplies an industry view alongside the weak small AAA sample. His actual MLBAM identity is 640449; the model never joins by the guessed similar ID 620443 or by a name alone. Together with Brinson he prevents the source review from considering only famous successful prospects. No later career disappointment enters the predictors, and a high ranking is not a promise of a full following-year job.
666160|2016: Moniak has 194 rookie PA, one HR, 35 strikeouts and eleven walks after his 2016 draft. The preseason top-100 list necessarily has no professional listing for this new entrant. His draft pedigree remains distinct evidence. The research dataset has two 2016 records with differing hit grades and ETA zero versus 2020, demonstrating why arbitrary first/last-row selection is unsafe. A later 2017 ranking cannot fill his 2016 slot. This case qualifies the meaning of an unlisted new draftee rather than rejecting pedigree or scouting generally.
608369|2016: Seager's rank-one preseason listing, after ranks seven and 34 in the preceding years, coexists with 687 MLB PA and 26 HR in 2016. This ordinary established case checks that the rank source does not fabricate future rookie eligibility or replace extensive MLB evidence. Current biography age/team/level on the page are intentionally excluded. The full-year workload remains the main observed opportunity signal; how strongly the fitted learner actually uses the old ranking must be checked after fitting, not assumed beneficial from rank one alone.
